# BasePart

- Inherits [`PVInstance`](pvinstance.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("BasePart")`
- **Abstract**: it cannot be created; other classes inherit from it

The abstract base class of every solid object in the world. A part has a position, an orientation, a size, a material and physical properties.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Anchored` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether this part is fixed in place. An anchored part is not moved by gravity, forces or collisions, but other parts still collide with it. Setting it keeps the part's position and orientation. |
| `AngularDamping` | `number` | `0.05` | read/write | How quickly this part stops spinning when nothing touches it, as the share of its spin that it loses each second. |
| `AngularVelocity` | `vector` | — | read/write | The angular velocity of this part in radians per second about each world axis, as of the last simulation tick. Setting it sets the spin for the next tick. |
| `AssemblyMass` | `number` | — | read-only | The total mass, in kilograms, of this part and every part rigidly joined to it by a `Weld` or a `FixedConstraint`. |
| `Buoyant` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether a `Water` pushes this part up. An unanchored part in water is lifted by the water it displaces, at several points across its shape, so a hull pitches and rolls; it is also slowed by the water's `Viscosity`. With it off, water ignores the part. |
| `CFrame` | `CFrame` | — | read/write | The position and orientation of this part in world space. It is stored in double precision; `Position` and `Orientation` are read from it. |
| `CanCollide` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this part blocks other parts. With it off, other parts pass through, but `Touched` still fires, which is how a trigger volume, a checkpoint or a pickup works. |
| `CanQuery` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether raycasts, shapecasts and overlap queries can find this part. It is independent of `CanCollide`: a part can block movement and still be ignored by a camera ray. |
| `CanTouch` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this part takes part in touch events. With it off, neither `Touched` nor `TouchEnded` fires for this part or for a part that touches it. Collisions are still resolved. Turn it off for scenery that no script listens to. |
| `CastShadow` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this part casts a shadow, from the sun and from every light. Turn it off for effects that should not darken the scene, such as a muzzle flash, a trail or a marker on the ground. The part is still drawn and lit, and still receives shadows. A transparent part casts no shadow regardless of this value. |
| `CollisionGroup` | `string` | `"Default"` | read/write | The name of the collision group that decides which parts this one collides with. Register groups with `PhysicsService:RegisterCollisionGroup`. Setting a name that is not registered raises an error. |
| `ContactDetails` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether `Collided` fires for this part. Off by default, because reporting every contact has a cost. |
| `Density` | `number` | `1` | read/write | The mass of this part per cubic meter, in kilograms. The part's `Mass` is its density times the volume of its shape. |
| `Dormancy` | `Enum.Dormancy` | `Enum.Dormancy.Auto` | read/write | Whether the part may sleep where no player is near. On a dedicated server, a `CharacterBody` with no player's focus within `dormant_radius` (`[server]` in `project.toml`; twice `StreamingService.LoadRadius` unless the game says) does not walk, and what it was asked to do (`Move`) waits until a player comes near. A player sees only within the load radius, so a character wakes before anybody can see it. `Never` keeps the part awake wherever it is.<br><br>A host and a single-player game never sleep anything, nor does a world one of whose players has no character or focus: that player is sent the whole world. |
| `Dormant` | `boolean` | — | read-only | Whether the part is asleep this tick because no player is near it (`Dormancy`). Decided where the physics step begins, from where the players were then. |
| `Fade` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How much this machine fades the part out of its own picture, from 0 to 1. At 0 the part is drawn as `Transparency` says; at 1 it is not drawn. It is never replicated and never saved, so use it to change what one player sees of a part that every player has, such as a tree between the camera and the character. The part keeps casting the shadow that its `Transparency` gives it. |
| `Friction` | `number` | `0.3` | read/write | How much this surface resists sliding, from 0 (no friction) to 1 (very grippy). A contact uses a combination of both surfaces' values, so one slippery part is enough to make a pair slide. |
| `LagCompensated` | `boolean` | `false` | read/write | Whether `Workspace:RaycastAsSeenBy` checks a shot against this part where the shooter's machine drew it, rather than where it is now. Every player's `Character` is checked that way without it. Set it on a moving target that is not a player's, such as an NPC, a vehicle or a dummy.<br><br>Only the authority reads it, and it is not replicated. |
| `LinearDamping` | `number` | `0.05` | read/write | How quickly this part slows down when nothing touches it, as the share of its speed that it loses each second. At 0 it never slows; 1 feels like moving through thick air. |
| `LinearVelocity` | `vector` | — | read/write | The velocity of this part in meters per second, as of the last simulation tick. Setting it sets the velocity for the next tick. To push the part instead of setting its velocity, use `ApplyImpulse`. |
| `Mass` | `number` | — | read-only | The mass of this part in kilograms: `Density` times the volume of its shape. Change `Density` or `Size` to change it. |
| `Material` | `Material?` | — | read/write | The material this part is drawn with: a material loaded with `Material.load`, a copy made with `material:Clone()`, or nil. With nil, the part uses the engine's default material, which is white, non-metallic and fairly rough.<br><br>A part has no color of its own. Its look comes from its material, and a part can change only the parameters that the material declares, with `SetMaterialParameter`. The default material declares `Color` and `Transparency`.<br><br>Reading this property returns the material itself, not a copy; call `material:Clone()` to get one you can change. A `MeshPart` with no material is drawn as its model file describes, tinted by a `Color` parameter if you set one. |
| `MaterialParameters` | `MaterialParameters` | — | read/write | The material parameters this part overrides, as a table keyed by name. Each read returns a new table that holds only the overridden values. The possible names are `Color`, `Transparency`, `Emissive`, `Metalness`, `Roughness`, `NormalScale` and `AlphaCutoff`.<br><br>An override that the current material does not declare is kept but has no effect, so a part looks the same after its material is changed and changed back. Prefer `SetMaterialParameter`, which checks the name against the material. Assigning this property replaces the whole set and checks only that each entry is a known parameter with a value of the right type. |
| `Orientation` | `vector` | — | read/write | The rotation of this part in world space, as angles in degrees about the Y, X and Z axes, applied in that order. |
| `PhaseCollision` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether this part's phase decides what it collides with. On, the default, it never collides with the characters and owned parts of players outside its phase, and does with those inside it. Off, it collides as any part does, and the game decides with `CollisionGroup` who stands on what. |
| `Position` | `vector` | — | read/write | The position of this part in world space, in meters. It is `CFrame`'s position rounded to single precision; more than a few kilometers from the origin, do your math on `CFrame` instead. |
| `ReceivesDecals` | `boolean` | `true` | read/write | Whether a `Decal` is drawn on this part. A decal projects onto everything inside its box; turn this off for parts that should stay clean, such as a character standing on a scorch mark. The decal still paints the surfaces around the part. Terrain always receives decals. |
| `ReplicationPriority` | `number` | `1` | read/write | How much this part's changes come first when a player's budget cannot carry every change at once (`Player.ReplicationBudget`). 1 by default; 3 makes the part's turn come three times as fast, 0.25 four times as slowly, and 0 only once a second. A part a player's machine waits for is drawn where it was last sent, moving smoothly between the states it was sent, a little behind.<br><br>Only the authority reads it, and it is not replicated. A part that does not change costs nothing, whatever its priority. |
| `Restitution` | `number` | `0` | read/write | How much this surface bounces, from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (a perfect bounce). A contact combines both surfaces' values, as it does for `Friction`. |
| `RollingResistance` | `number` | `0.01` | read/write | How much a round part resists rolling while it touches something: it slows steadily, by this many times the strength of gravity, until it stops. 0.01 is a hard ball on wood, 0.001 a steel ball on steel and 0.05 a ball on carpet. A ball, a cylinder and a capsule are slowed by it, and a part of another shape is not. 0 turns it off. |
| `Size` | `vector` | — | read/write | The size of this part in meters, along its own X, Y and Z axes. |

## Methods

### `ApplyAngularImpulse(impulse: vector)`

Applies an instant twist about the axis the vector points along, in kilogram square meters per second. It changes the part's spin without moving it. It takes effect at the next simulation tick.

### `ApplyImpulse(impulse: vector)`

Applies an instant push at the part's center of mass, in kilogram meters per second. It takes effect at the next simulation tick. An anchored part ignores it.

### `ApplyImpulseAtPosition(impulse: vector, position: vector)`

Applies an instant push at a point in world space, in kilogram meters per second. A push away from the center of mass also turns the part. It takes effect at the next simulation tick.

### `BindToPredictedTouch(fn: (character: BasePart, step: PredictedStep) -> ())`

Runs `fn(character, step)` inside the simulation step when a player's character that this machine simulates starts touching this part. Use it for a jump pad, a booster or a trampoline, so the effect is predicted on the player's machine and needs no correction.

On a client the function runs again for each tick that is replayed after a correction, as a function bound with `RunService:BindToPredictedStep` does. A part has one such function; binding again replaces it. The function must not yield.

### `ClearMaterialParameter(name: string)`

Removes this part's override of one material parameter, so the part uses the material's value again. Does nothing if the parameter is not overridden.

### `Fracture(options: { Pieces: number?, Seed: number?, Strength: number? }? = nil): Model`

Breaks the part into pieces and returns them in a `Model` where the part was. The part is destroyed. Each piece is a part like the original, held to the pieces beside it by a `FixedConstraint` that breaks under `Strength` newtons, so the pieces stand together until something hits them hard enough. The pieces are unanchored. A part that was anchored keeps its footing: an anchored `Footing` part under its bottom, which does not collide, holds the pieces along the bottom by the same joints, so a wall breaks where it is hit rather than falling over whole.

`options.Pieces` is how many, from 1 to 64 (8 by default). `options.Seed` chooses the cut: the same seed and the same part give the same pieces on every machine. `options.Strength` is what each joint holds; by default it is twice the part's weight.

The pieces are simulation: in a match the server's, sent to every player as parts, so use as few as the moment needs. Dust and small chips are better as a `ParticleEmitter` burst when a joint breaks: drawn on each machine and sent as nothing but the burst.

Only a `Part` whose `Shape` is `Block` can be broken.

### `GetMaterialParameter(name: string): (Color3 | number | Vector2 | vector | { number })?`

Returns the value this part is drawn with for one material parameter: the part's override if it has one, otherwise the material's own value. Returns nil for a surface shader parameter that neither sets; the shader's default is then used.

### `GetNetworkOwner(): Player?`

Returns the player whose machine simulates this part, or nil if the authority does. On a client it returns the local `Player` for a part that client owns, and nil for every other part.

### `GetRenderCFrame(): CFrame`

Returns where this part is drawn in the current frame, which is between its positions at the last two simulation ticks. Use it for anything that must line up with the picture, such as a camera that follows the part.

It differs from `CFrame` only inside a render step: a function bound with `RunService:BindToRenderStep`, a `PreRender` handler, or an action whose context has `Rate = Render`. Everywhere else, including on a server, it returns `CFrame`, so simulation code never depends on frame timing.

### `SetMaterialParameter(name: string, value: Color3 | number | boolean | Vector2 | vector | { number })`

Overrides one parameter of this part's material, for this part only. Raises an error if the material does not declare the parameter. `Color` and `Emissive` take a `Color3`; the other built-in parameters take a number.

A parameter of the material's surface shader can be set if the material lists it in `instanceParameters`. It takes a number, a boolean, a `Vector2`, a `vector`, a `Color3`, or a table of four numbers, but not a texture. Surface shader parameters are not replicated: set them on the machine that draws the part.

### `SetNetworkOwner(player: Player?)`

Gives one player's machine the simulation of this part. That machine simulates the part and sends its position, so what the player pushes moves immediately on their screen. Pass nil to return the part to the authority.

Only the authority can call it, and only on an unanchored part. When a player leaves, the parts they owned return to the authority. The owner's results are trusted: validate them, or do not hand the part over, if cheating matters.

### `UnbindFromPredictedTouch()`

Removes the function bound with `BindToPredictedTouch`. Does nothing if none is bound.

## Events

Signals are deferred: a handler runs at the next resumption point, not
inside the call that fired the signal.

### `Collided(otherPart: BasePart, position: vector, normal: vector, speed: number)`

Fires together with `Touched` when `ContactDetails` is on, with details of the contact. Passes the other part, the contact point in world space, the direction from this part into the other, and the speed at which the two were approaching along that direction, in meters per second, before the collision was resolved.

### `TouchEnded(otherPart: BasePart)`

Fires when another part stops touching this one. Passes the other part. It does not fire for contacts that end because a part was destroyed.

### `Touched(otherPart: BasePart)`

Fires when another part starts touching this one. Passes the other part. A pair that stays in contact fires once, not every tick. Like every signal, it is deferred: handlers run at the next resumption point, not inside the physics step.
